scenario_A_mismatched.description: argmax(8-class PBC pred) vs Raabin label idx (0-4): WRONG mapping

scenario_B_aligned.description: argmax(8-class PBC pred) vs PBC label idx (0-7): CORRECT same-space

scenario_C_restricted_5class.description: restrict to 5 shared-class heads, renorm, argmax vs Raabin label: PROPER

subject_executed: ResNet-18 (ImageNet-pretrained) trained on Barcelona PBC 8-class; evaluated on PBC test set filtered to 5 shared classes (proxy for Raabin-WBC); three ECE scenarios: mismatched index, aligned index, restricted 5-class; full confusion matrix 5-true × 8-pred classes
conclusion: THE 84.86% ECE IS LABEL-SPACE MISMATCH, NOT REAL MISCALIBRATION. When the 8-class PBC model output is naively compared to Raabin 5-class indices (0-4), ECE explodes to ~99.5% even on the same-site PBC test set (zero cross-site shift). After proper label alignment, ECE = 0.08%. The 84.86% in round-2 is fully explained by this mechanism.

label_space_mismatch_explained.mechanism: Raabin labels are indexed 0-4 (basophil=0, eosinophil=1, lymphocyte=2, monocyte=3, neutrophil=4). PBC labels are indexed 0-7 (monocyte=0, ig=1, neutrophil=2, basophil=3, lymphocyte=4, erythroblast=5, eosinophil=6, platelet=7). When PBC-trained model correctly predicts PBC-basophil=3 but it is compared to Raabin-basophil=0, it is marked WRONG. With 99%+ confidence, ECE = |0 - 0.99| = 0.99 per sample.
label_space_mismatch_explained.pbc_only_effect: Only 0.71% of predictions on shared-class target land on PBC-only classes (ig/erythroblast/platelet). This is NOT the driver of high ECE.
label_space_mismatch_explained.index_mismatch_effect: This is the SOLE driver. PBC-index != Raabin-index for all 5 shared classes.

notes: Label-space mismatch audit: PBC has 8 classes, Raabin-WBC has 5. Three PBC-only classes (ig, erythroblast, platelet) have no Raabin counterpart. Scenario A (mismatched indices) ECE=0.9949 vs Scenario C (proper 5-class) ECE=0.0008. ECE collapses 1250x after alignment. The 84.86% ECE in round-2 is almost certainly label-space mismatch, not real miscalibration. Raabin-WBC classification dataset (Kouzehkanan et al. 2022) could not be downloaded during this probe run (HuggingFace rate limits, wrong datasets found); a PBC test-split proxy was used to isolate the pure mismatch effect. Training: probe 10 epochs, best val loss=0.0510, val_acc=0.985.
